Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed opacity occupying the lower half of the right hemithorax, which obscures the right hemidiaphragm and cardiac border. In an asymptomatic young adult, this presentation is characteristic of a giant solitary fibrous tumor of the pleura, for which surgical resection is the standard management due to the mass's size and potential for compression or malignant transformation.
